I am sixty-five years old and have never been to school, but I have farmed these six *mu* in Quzhou County for over fifty years. In this part of Hebei, the land is good for one thing: wheat in the winter and maize in the summer. That is what I will plant this year on all my land. I will buy improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed from the local dealer, because the old traditional varieties do not yield enough to feed my family and leave grain to sell. For the wheat, I will rotary-till the field before sowing in autumn, and I will irrigate four times—winter water, green-turn water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. For the maize, there is no time to till after the wheat harvest in early June; I will sow directly into the wheat stubble to catch the summer heat, and irrigate twice—once right after sowing and once when the plants flare their leaves. I will spread compound fertilizer at sowing for both crops, and top-dress extra nitrogen on the wheat when it greens up in spring. I will spray for insects, weeds, and diseases about four times on the wheat and three times on the maize. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg of wheat per *mu* and 550 kg of maize per *mu*, which is what my neighbors and I usually get around here.
